title: QosPanel.open's null guard is dead-on-arrival — the typed Dictionary assignment throws first, per this diff's own comment
evidence:
+func open(pipe_id: int, sim: SimCore) -> void:
+	_pipe_id = pipe_id
+	var p: Dictionary = sim.pipes.get(pipe_id)
+	if p == null:
+		close_panel()
+		return
--- and, in the same diff, scripts/sim/sim_core.gd:---
+	# UNTYPED on purpose: routes.get(missing) yields null, and a typed
+	# Dictionary local throws a SCRIPT ERROR on the assignment itself —
+	# which silently aborted callers and left the null guard below dead.
+	var r = routes.get(dst)
detail: sim_core's own comment says a typed Dictionary local 'throws a SCRIPT ERROR on the assignment itself', leaving its null guard dead. open() repeats exactly the pattern the same diff documents as broken.
recommended_fix: Untype the local — var p = sim.pipes.get(pipe_id) — matching _pick_next_pipe; keep the null guard.
